A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Quantization without Tears study. Their main text, equations, thirteen tables, four figures, and appendices A–B are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original QwT experiments on image classification, detection, segmentation, multimodal recognition, image generation, and language tasks, including appendix results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and reports corrected ResNet results and additional explicitly distinguished quantization settings in Table 11.

M1.justification: The linear compensation modules, closed-form initialization, sequential compensation procedure, and optional fine-tuning remain unchanged. The Percentile configuration correction does not introduce a change to QwT.

E1.justification: All datasets, tasks, and domains are retained. The expanded ResNet bit-width combinations change model configurations within the existing ImageNet classification evaluation, not dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison methods remain unchanged. Table 11 removes several CL-Calib rows containing only missing-result dashes; its scored CL-Calib comparisons remain. These deletions do not remove evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The ResNet classification conditions receive a substantial correction: results labeled 4/4 and 6/6 in v3 used 4/8 and 6/8 weight/activation precision. v4 supplies true 4/4 and 6/6 results and distinguishes all four configurations across ResNet-18, ResNet-50, and ResNet-101 in Table 11. This repairs the conditions underlying the matched-precision comparisons; calibration procedures and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Expanded Table 11 enables a limited activation-precision sensitivity comparison at fixed weight precision: 4/4 versus 4/8 and 6/6 versus 6/8 across three ResNets. Existing PTQ/QAT compatibility analyses and generated-image case studies are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for these results. The revision retains the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 11 replace the mislabeled ResNet results with correct 4/4 and 6/6 values, retaining the earlier values under 4/8 and 6/8 in Table 11. For example, ResNet-50 QwT* was listed as 75.8 at 4/4; the corrected 4/4 result is 72.5, below CL-Calib's unchanged 75.4. This materially changes the apparent matched-precision ranking, rather than demonstrating a same-setting performance decline. Other results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The quantization definitions, compensation formulation, closed-form regression solution in Equations 1–6, and associated mathematical reasoning are unchanged. No assumptions, proofs, or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about QwT's speed, accuracy, simplicity, generality, and structural compensation paradigm.

C2.justification: The new Correction Note attributes the erroneous ResNet comparisons to a Percentile implementation/configuration-label issue and states that conclusions remain unaffected. Section 4.1 also drops CL-Calib from the citations supporting its six-bit state-of-the-art alignment statement. Other interpretations and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The Correction Note newly documents the actual activation precision behind the earlier Percentile results and explains the configuration-label error. Appendix A's implementation instructions, calibration sizes, fine-tuning hyperparameters, hardware information, and code access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 4.1 removes CL-Calib [47] from the prior methods cited for six-bit accuracy alignment, leaving IGQ-ViT [38]. This is a limited correction to comparison positioning; the related-work discussion and all 56 bibliography entries are otherwise unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 adds a standalone Correction Note before the references and expands Table 11's caption. The remaining prose and section sequence are essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 11 expands to four precision groups per ResNet, removes empty comparator rows, gains a longer caption, and moves onto its own page. References and appendix material consequently reflow. All four figures retain their content; Tables 9–10 are repositioned without substantive display changes.

improvement.justification: v4 improves the reliability and transparency of the ResNet evidence by acknowledging the configuration error and separating genuine 4/4 and 6/6 results from the earlier 8-bit-activation results. This prevents misleading matched-precision comparisons. The improvement is limited by unchanged discussion: Section 4.1 still claims superiority in nearly all cases without fully reconciling the corrected ResNet results below CL-Calib. The method and remaining empirical evidence are unchanged.
